chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Tatum answers Forsythe with scales and a diminished run
summary: Tatum sits down, tests the keyboard, runs scales with one finger and a diminished chord with another.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

know, and waited.
So finally, Tatum came in. He had little tables in there, so we sent Tatum a drink and he started walking... So he talked about England, and he said, 'Oh, I've heard you,' and Tatum said, 'I've heard about your composition'... He had several. He was very popular while he was here. His works...bands were playing them...

So he said, 'I want to hear you play.' Tatum said, 'What would you like to hear?' I don't remember what it was. But Tatum sat down, and in his usual way, as I said before... He sits down at the piano, and first he starts to get the range of the keyboard, the familiarity with his fingers, you know, puts his fingers (?). So he takes his left hand and [SOUND OF LEFT HAND FLYING] and then [WRHRAAP] with the right hand. Then he brings them together, you know, running...
Now, Tatum can run a scale with one finger. I said, 'Let me see you do it on a diminished chord,' and he runs this diminished chord one finger... And I mean, he would...

Yes. [SINGS IT] ...with one finger! Now, I didn't want to ask him, because I felt embarrassed for him. I figured if I asked him to do it with another finger, I'd be embarrassed, so I didn't ask him. But he just went into
it with the other finger! I said "My God."
